raw_response:
Ai, sit down, let me tell you how I'm thinking about this year.

I'm 65 now. Forty years working this same ten mu of ground — my father's ground before me. Middle school is all the schooling I got, but the extension fellow from the county comes around sometimes and I listen. I don't write things down. I remember.

Nine people in the household. Two of my sons are working construction in Shijiazhuang and the granddaughter is at the county middle school. So on the farm it's really me, my wife, and my daughter-in-law most days. The boys come back for wheat harvest and cotton picking if we need them. With their wages coming in, we're not starving, but I still watch every yuan on fertilizer and diesel. Ten mu doesn't feed nine people on grain alone — the off-farm money is what really keeps us going.

**The land.** Seven mu on the east side is my wheat-maize ground. Heavier soil, holds water. I've been doing wheat-maize double crop there for twenty-some years, same as everyone in the village. The other three point one mu on the west is sandier — my father planted cotton there, and I still do. Cotton likes that lighter soil and it gives me cash in the fall when everyone else is just selling grain.

**Wheat.** I'll plant around October 10th, after I clear the maize stubble. I save some of my own seed — Jimai variety, been growing it five or six years, does fine — and buy maybe 30 jin of fresh seed to mix in. Before the wheel planter goes through, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 kind, fifty jin. Then in spring when it greens up and starts jointing, I topdress about 20 jin of urea per mu. The extension guy tells us 15 kg N is enough but I've always done a little more — maybe 17, 18. A bag costs what it costs; I'd rather have the yield than save five yuan and watch the wheat turn yellow. I water three times: once after winter comes back in February, once at jointing in April, and once when the grain is filling in May. Spray herbicide in March, and if I see rust spots I'll spray tebuconazole. Expect around 450 jin per mu on a normal year. Last year I got 470 — good rain.

**Maize.** As soon as the combine is off the wheat in early June, I go straight in with the maize planter. One week window, no time to waste. I buy hybrid seed every year — Zhengdan 958 or whichever variety the seed shop has, about 70 yuan per mu. The planter drops seed and compound fertilizer together, about 40 jin of compound per mu. Then at the big trumpet stage in late July I topdress urea, about 25 jin per mu. If it doesn't rain by early August I'll water once. Corn borer shows up most years — I spray once. Expect 500 jin per mu. Family labor mostly; the young ones come back to help load sacks.

**Cotton.** Three point one mu, plant mid-to-late April. I buy Bt cotton seed, about 40 yuan per mu. Cotton needs more fuss than grain — I spread compound fertilizer before planting, about 40 jin per mu, and then topdress again when flowering starts in July. Maybe 13 kg N total per mu. I water twice in July and August when it's dry. Spraying — this is the work with cotton. I go through the field five, six times with insecticide for bollworm and aphids. Picking is all by hand, three rounds from late August into October. My wife and daughter-in-law pick most of it, boys come back for the last round. Expect about 250 jin of lint per mu. Price was decent last year, 6 yuan a jin or so.

**Budget.** Counting seed, fertilizer, pesticide, diesel for the pump, I'll spend maybe 4,500 yuan total on inputs across the ten mu. That's about what I spent last year. I don't take loans — pay cash, always have.
